title: Greedy bases and relational complexity of diagonal type groups
summary: A base for a subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Sym}(Ω)$ is a sequence of elements of $Ω$ with trivial pointwise stabiliser. The size of the smallest base for $G$ is denoted $b(G)$. There is a natural greedy algorithm to compute a base for $G$, and it was conjectured by Cameron in 1999 that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that if $G$ is primitive then any base returned by this algorithm has size at most $cb(G)$. In this paper we determine the size of every base returned by the greedy algorithm when $G$ is a primitive group of diagonal type, and hence prove Cameron's conjecture for these…
